news.title: Netflix secures 2030 World Cup rights in Spain and Andorra
news.lede: Netflix has acquired the broadcasting rights for the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra, the platform announced on Tuesday. Under the deal, the streaming service will show all 104 of the tournament's matches live. The 2030 World Cup is scheduled to take place across Morocco, Portugal, and Spain, with three special centenary celebration matches also set to be held in Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. The move marks a significant step in Netflix's strategy to expand its portfolio of live sports events and to compete with traditional television broadcasters.

news.title: Netflix secures 2030 FIFA World Cup rights in Spain and Andorra | Football News
news.lede: The American streaming giant Netflix has secured the exclusive audiovisual rights to the 2030 men’s FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra. It will stream all 104 matches of the competition, which involves 48 teams. The agreement, announced on October 13, 2026, allows Netflix to expand its live sports portfolio. This is also the first time it will be streaming a major international men’s football tournament in Spain, one of the host nations for the event.The exclusivity of the deal does not mean that all matches will be accessible only to subscribers.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president received payment of £1.3m from World Cup company
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under more pressure to resign after it was revealed he received £1.3m in 2024 on top of his salary. FIFA has committed to publishing Infantino's salary, bonus and allowances in its annual report every year since 2016. For 2024, he reported £3.88m ($5.1m) in salary but US tax filings show he also received £1.3m ($1.76m) from FWC2026, the company set up to organise and run this summer's World Cup, which was not publicly disclosed by FIFA in the annual report. Article 43, paragraph 13 of FIFA's statutes reads: "The individual compensation of the FIFA president, the members of the council and the FIFA secretary general shall be made public."

news.title: Netflix secures rights to air 2030 World Cup in Spain, Andorra
news.lede: Netflix said on Tuesday it had secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain, which is co-hosting the tournament, and Andorra. It would be Netflix's first broadcast of a major men's international tournament in Spain, the company said. The 2026 World Cup was aired there by national channel TVE. California-based Netflix did not disclose financial terms.

news.title: Netflix secures 2030 World Cup TV rights in Spain
news.lede: Spain won their second men's World Cup this year. Streaming platform Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Andorra. It is the first time the subscription-based platform will show the men's World Cup. "We will offer all 104 matches of the world's biggest football competition live," Netflix said in a statement.

news.title: Netflix makes first major entry into live men’s football with World Cup deal
news.lede: Netflix has made its first major entry into live men’s football by snapping up exclusive rights to the 2030 World Cup in Spain, home of the co-hosts and holders. The agreement builds on the global streaming giant’s deal with Fifa for the exclusive rights in North America to show the next two editions of the Women’s World Cup. It means the 2030 World Cup – uniquely being shared across Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with South American staging the opening matches – will mostly be behind a paywall in one of the primary host countries. Netflix will make “one match per matchday” available for free in Spain, adding that a “package of matches, including every Spain match, both semi-finals and the final, will be made available for broadcast on a national free-to-air broadcaster, ensuring broad accessibility for audiences across the country”.

news.title: Netflix secures rights to air 2030 World Cup in Spain
news.lede: Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra, marking its first coverage of a major men’s international football tournament in Spain. The streaming platform announced the deal on Tuesday but did not disclose the financial terms. Under the agreement, one match per matchday will be available to watch free in Spain. Netflix will also offer a free-to-air channel showing selected matches, including all Spain’s games, both semi-finals and the final.
